reuse.why: Holidays are added to the existing shared applyWeekendRule, which every date path (getNextDate, upcoming dates, dates in range, schedule templates) already calls; parseRecurDate just forwards the field.

duplication.why: The off-day test is defined once inside applyWeekendRule and the before/after branches are folded into one stepping loop; nothing is copied.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts, the look-around windows stay in server/schedules/app.ts and the type in models/schedule.ts, matching the tree's layering.

scope.why: Only the weekend rule, the data plumbing, the search windows it affects and focused tests are changed.

maintainability.why: The design is easy to own; the occurrence-window padding (HOLIDAY_SHIFT_DAYS times the holiday count, take + holidays length) is a heuristic a maintainer has to reason about.

bypasses_abstraction.where: No path decides off days on its own; all go through applyWeekendRule.

disguised_duplication.where: None; the old nextMonday/previousFriday branches were replaced, not kept beside the new loop.

one_place.where: applyWeekendRule in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts (isOffDay), used by getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, getDatesInRange and the schedule-template helpers.
